content.text:
Plain, dependency-free web stack — no framework, no build step:

- **HTML** — single file, semantic markup for nav/hero/card/stats
- **CSS** — plain CSS3 in a `<style>` block: flexbox/grid for layout, CSS custom properties for the color palette, `@media` queries for responsiveness, and CSS 3D transforms (`perspective`, `rotateX/rotateY`) for the mouse-tilt effect
- **JavaScript** — vanilla JS (no libraries), split into a few IIFEs:
  - Deploy-progress loop (`requestAnimationFrame` driving the progress bar/timer)
  - The network map itself: **HTML5 Canvas 2D** for the dotted landmasses, arcs, particles, hub glow, and radar sweep, plus a handful of DOM elements (`.net-pill`) absolutely-positioned over the canvas for the flag/label pills, since crisp text and pill styling is easier in HTML/CSS than canvas
  - Country flags are drawn with pure CSS gradients (no images, no emoji — Windows doesn't reliably render flag emoji)

So it's literally just [index.html](index.html) — open it directly in a browser, no npm install, no bundler, nothing to compile. That was a deliberate choice for a single landing page: zero build tooling, portable, and easy for you to drop straight onto any static host or CMS.

Summary of this iteration on [index.html](index.html) — same dependency-free HTML/CSS/JS, no rebuild:

**Composition restructure**
- Dropped the grid-locked hero layout; the network now spans from roughly the horizontal center of the hero to just past the right edge (slightly overflowing, clipped naturally by the hero's overflow), and top-to-bottom of the hero — a major visual element, not a background decoration.
- The floating server card is back (280–320px, glass/translucent, blurred, blue/purple shadow), absolutely positioned to genuinely overlap the network rather than sit in its own column.
- Fixed a layout bug from this change: the stats-bar section was accidentally inheriting the hero's new `min-height`, producing a huge blank gap — split into its own `.stats-wrap` class.

**Network graphic**
- Singapore hub is now dramatically more prominent: layered blue→purple ambient disc, a rotating dashed orbital ring, 3 expanding pulse rings, and a bright white-hot core — verified positioned at its real lon/lat (I'd briefly hand-placed markers for "visual balance" per your detailed spec, then reverted after your follow-up that the map/label positions weren't earth-accurate — hub and all 7 destinations now use the same real-coordinate projection as the dotted landmasses, so nothing is arbitrarily placed).
- Routes are thicker (1.8px core + soft glow pass), blue→purple gradient, each with its own curvature bias so they sweep organically instead of symmetrically, 2-3 flowing particles per route.
- Dot map: increased density/brightness generally, plus extra brightness concentrated around the hub and each destination.
- Added a true 3D perspective floor grid (converging vertical lines + eased horizontal depth lines) — per your follow-up, this got a static resting tilt (`rotateX/rotateY`) rather than mouse-interactive, since you asked to remove the mouse-tilt behavior.
- Fixed the Australia flag badge, which was rendering as a stray "+" icon.

**Left side / CTA**
- Bigger headline (64px), more breathing room.
- Replaced the yellow/orange lightning emoji with a white inline-SVG bolt icon.

**One open item**: there's no existing Nxeon logo file anywhere in this project folder — I kept the gradient "N" mark placeholder. If you have an actual logo (SVG/PNG), send it over and I'll wire it into the header in place of the mark.
